items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: So they called me Pig, you know, 'Goodby, Pig, I'm going away.'

ctx.x: Okay. All right. 1895. Well, I went to Auction Street School -- what school I went to. Went to Auction Street School, and my school teacher was getting ready -- a lady had let her child come from Chicago to Memphis. And the lady wouldn't let the child -- let my school teacher bring her back to Chicago. So my school teacher had a pass that this child had come from Chicago to Memphis on. And so she -- I had just been to the store for my mother, and she said, "Well, goodby," -- they called me Pig, you know, "Goodby,…

my mother. I ran up the street, like I was going to ask my mother, and I came back and told her my mother said it was all right, I could go. So she said she was going to get on the train. She told me where to meet her down the street, so I met her down on the street, and we went down to the station. And I had on some blue shoes, some red shoes and a blue dress. And so she took me on into the station, and the man hollared, "All out for the northbound trains."
